headline: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
summary: Researchers demonstrated that on AMD and some Intel PCs, opening the case allows resetting the TPM lockout, enabling attackers to guess short Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs.
whyItMatters: Resetting TPM lockout undermines the security of Windows authentication mechanisms.
recommendedAction: Enforce longer, complex PINs and consider physical tamper protection.

headline: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
summary: The Java4Shell vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑114938) permits unauthenticated remote code execution in several Java‑based applications, affecting Java 17.0.6+ on AVX‑512 VBMI‑capable CPUs.
whyItMatters: Pre‑auth RCE can let attackers take over critical development and CI/CD tools.
recommendedAction: Apply the vendor patches and upgrade Java to a non‑vulnerable version.

headline: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
summary: Apache issued security updates to fix a critical Roller vulnerability that attackers are actively exploiting to achieve remote code execution on vulnerable servers.
whyItMatters: Active exploitation can lead to full server compromise.
recommendedAction: Apply the Apache Roller patches immediately.

headline: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
summary: CISA added a critical CVE‑2026‑115731 RCE vulnerability in Perforce Puppet to its KEV catalog, noting active exploitation of the IaC platform.
whyItMatters: Exploitation of Puppet can allow attackers to control enterprise infrastructure.
recommendedAction: Patch Puppet immediately and review configuration for signs of compromise.

headline: From Deepfakes to Helpdesk Impersonation: Why Stronger Verification Matters
summary: Attackers are leveraging deepfakes and helpdesk impersonation to trick employees into granting system access. Specops Software outlines how stronger identity verification can mitigate these social‑engineering attacks.
whyItMatters: Social‑engineering attacks can lead to unauthorized system compromise.
recommendedAction: Implement multi‑factor verification for all support requests.

headline: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
summary: A suspected Chinese APT group has rebuilt the EggStreme malware toolkit, continuously changing file hashes and domains to evade detection while targeting Philippine government organizations.
whyItMatters: Evolving malware can bypass existing defenses and threaten critical government systems.
recommendedAction: Update detection signatures and monitor for new EggStreme indicators.

headline: AI Pentesting Checklist for Web Apps: 15 Questions to Ask Before Choosing a Vendor
summary: The article provides a checklist of 15 questions to evaluate AI‑based web‑app pentesting vendors, emphasizing coverage, logged‑in flow testing, and production safety.
whyItMatters: Choosing an inadequate AI pentesting vendor can leave critical vulnerabilities untested.
recommendedAction: Use the checklist to assess vendor capabilities before purchase.

headline: Dizigom illegal streaming service with 21M monthly visits shuts down
summary: The Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment announced the shutdown of Dizigom, a major Turkish piracy site, following a settlement with its operators.
whyItMatters: Closing large piracy platforms reduces illegal distribution of copyrighted content.
recommendedAction: Monitor for successor sites and enforce anti‑piracy measures.

headline: Microsoft announces Windows Server 2028 with hardened security
summary: Microsoft announced Windows Server 2028, the next major server OS release, featuring hardened security controls.
whyItMatters: New server platform may impact planning and migration strategies.
recommendedAction: Review the announced features and begin compatibility testing.
